messages:
samir: Quick heads up 1:30 UTC deploy window for py/ts SDKs. Intend to publish py 0.13.0 and ts 2.4.0 behind dist-tags: npm -> 'canary-2.4.0', pip -> 'canary-0.13.0'. Shadow 3% traffic. Any blockers?

jess: CI flake on wheels signing earlier. I reran the job and keys look ok but the signer rotated last week. Recommend verifying wheel signatures before promoting.

deploy-bot: Canary publish scheduled at 1756009900. Jobs: publish-py, publish-ts, verify-signatures, smoke. CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/1756009900

nina: Reminder: we have enterprise customers pinned to 0.12.x - if things go sideways we'll need to serve a pinned fallback from internal registry. ops-lia can you confirm fallback artifacts exist?

ops-lia: Confirmed: fallback artifacts present: pip -> redwood-sdk==0.12.7-prod, npm -> @redwood/sdk@2.3.5. Internal registry TTLs refreshed. If we need to pin-back we can flip registry symlink in ~30s.

qa-bot: smoke-runner: streaming-connectivity.test FAILED on canary cohort during dry-run. Error: "connect: ECONNRESET" (see logs)

jess: Ugh, seeing the same on local smoke harness. Looks like reconnect loop introduced by the streaming backpressure change.

samir: How bad? numbers?

qa-bot: reconnects increased from avg 0.2/min to 4.5/min for the canary cohort. Error rate delta +1.2% on embeddings route.

nina: Given customer impact on streaming, propose we don't fully unpublish artifacts (so customers who opt-in can try) but we pin default dist-tags back to stable. i.e., remove 'latest' pointing to canary and set fallback tags. Safer than full yank. Thoughts?

jess: That seems reasonable. Avoids breaking enterprise pinned installs. We should still revoke canary dist-tags to avoid accidental pulls.

samir: Agree. Action: untag canary as default but keep artifacts in registry with canary label. ops-lia can you run the commands? Add a pip index removal only if we need a hard yank.

ops-lia: Running commands now: ```npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk latest || true
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk 2.3.5
python -m pip index versions redwood-sdk || true
# leaving canary wheels in internal registry under 'canary-0.13.0' namespace
```

deploy-bot: Dist-tag update executed at 1756009950. Traffic repointed to prod (no rollback of artifacts). Smoke-runner requeued.

qa-bot: Re-run smoke: streaming-connectivity.test still shows elevated reconnects (2.1/min) but error delta back down to +0.4%.

jess: So flake reduced but not fixed. Recommend holding off full GA until backpressure fix merged. We should also add a compatibility blurb in release notes about streaming behavior change and explicit migration steps.

docs-kate: Will draft release notes: include canary summary, rollback/pinback steps taken, and deprecation blurb for legacy sync client with a 60-day sunset. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2045 (will update after final).

nina: For deprecation timeline: suggest 60 days with opt-out instructions and SDK migration guide link. Also add a code snippet for clients to pin version in requirements.txt and package.json.

samir: Good. Also create an internal post in #customers to warn account teams if customers report issues. Ops: please keep registry TTLs extended for 72h.

ops-lia: Done. Extended TTLs and added a temporary redirect rule: if user agent contains "enterprise-upgrade", serve 2.3.5.

jess: One more ask: add a quick check to publish pipeline to enforce wheel signature verification and fail fast on unknown key ids. I'll open a follow-up PR to CI.

samir: Thanks everyone. Plan summary: untag canary from latest (done), keep canary artifacts in internal registry, pin default dist-tags back to stable, hold GA until fix merged (target re-run tomorrow 14:00 UTC), docs PR + deprecation notice in flight. Move postmortem to #postmortems if impact > 1% customers.

docs-kate: Draft created and assigned to samir for review.

jess: I'll pick up the CI signer PR.

nina: I'll notify account leads.

ops-lia: Monitoring registry & traffic for next 2h.
